title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (n° 120 ff. of the continuation of the Longue Marche). Let Π = Π_{0,3}^ be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞} over Q̄, and let M = M^ = Π^ab ≃ Ẑ(1)^3/diag, of rank 2 over Ẑ. The group Γ = Γ_Q × S_3 acts on M: Γ_Q through the cyclotomic character, and S_3 by permuting the three punctures. The image of Γ in Aut(M) is Γ̃ ≃ Ẑ^* × S_3.

Let M̃ be the arithmetic fundamental group of the quotient stack (P^1−{0,1,∞}, S_3)_Q modulo the commutator subgroup [Π,Π]. It is an extension of Γ by M. On the previous page Grothendieck considered quotients M̃ → M̃̃ such that:
- (a) M injects into M̃̃;
- (b) Γ' = M̃̃/M acts faithfully on M, so Γ' ≃ Γ̃;
- (c) the extension of Γ̃ by M is split.
For such a quotient, the set E of splittings is acted on by M̃ via conjugation. The relations (292) make E an M-torsor, i.e. any two splittings are conjugate by exactly one element of M. This uses H^0(Γ̃,M) = 0 together with the vanishing of the relevant H^1.

This page recalls that in the previous number the extension G_{ρ,σ} of Γ̃ by M^ was shown to be trivial. Two splittings were shown to be conjugate by one and only one element of M, and this existence-and-uniqueness of conjugation is the geometric content of (292). Earlier he had also built a surjection from π1(M_{0,3}) (abelianized) onto G̃_{ρ,σ}, making G̃ a quotient of M̃ with properties a), b), c).

Hence, up to unique isomorphism, one gets an object of the category of X'. Equivalently, one gets a pro-covering of the stack (M_{0,3,Q}, S_3)_s ≃ M'_{1,1,Q} (the λ-line modulo S_3, i.e. M_{1,1} rigidified by ±1). After forgetting the S_3-action and extending the base to Q̄, this pro-covering becomes the universal abelian pro-covering of P^1 − 3 points.

The page then turns to the Fermat tower x^n + y^n = 1. This is an explicit Q-rational, S_3-equivariant model of that universal abelian covering, hence another such object. The next page reports two things:
- Without the Fermat tower he would not have suspected that the extension of S_3 by M^ is semidirect.
- He conjectures that the two objects (the group-theoretic one and the Fermat one) are isomorphic, by a unique isomorphism.
He then computes the splitting classes via the Hochschild–Serre sequence: H^1(Γ, M^) ≃ H^0(Γ_Q, H^1(S_3, M^)).

Purpose: understand the 'abelian (metabelian) layer' of the Galois action on π1(P^1−3 points) together with the S_3 symmetry, as the first step of the Teichmüller-tower/GT program. The goal is a canonical, S_3-compatible rational model of the universal abelian cover.
errors: There is a potential tension, not resolved on this page. Making the splittings an M-torsor needs H^1(Γ̃, M) = 0 (with H^0 = 0). Yet the next page computes H^1(Γ, M^) ≃ H^0(Γ_Q, H^1(S_3, M^)), which can be nonzero: H^1(S_3, M) for the rank-2 A_2-type lattice is a small 3-torsion group. So uniqueness of splittings up to M-conjugation may hold for Γ̃ but not naively for Γ_Q × S_3, or (292) must encode a specific vanishing. The page does not make this distinction explicit.
The phrase 'à isomorphisme unique près' presupposes H^0(Γ̃, M) = 0. This is fine because Ẑ^* acts via the cyclotomic character, but it is not stated here.

ideas.what: Classifying quotients of the abelianized arithmetic π1 of (P^1−3 pts)/S_3 that split over the image Ẑ^*×S_3, with the splittings forming an M-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on π1^ab / metabelian quotient of P^1−{0,1,∞}; splitting of the abelianized fundamental-group extension
λ-line as level-2 cover of the moduli of elliptic curves; M_{0,4}/S_3 vs M_{1,1}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} as the basic pieces

ideas.what: Fermat tower as an explicit Q-rational, S_3-equivariant model of the universal abelian pro-covering of P^1−3 points; this model reveals that the extension of S_3 by M^ is semidirect
ideas.modern_name: Fermat tower and Galois action on its homology (Jacobi sums); Ihara's universal power series for Jacobi sums

ideas.what: Conjecture that the group-theoretically constructed object coincides, by a unique isomorphism, with the Fermat-tower object
ideas.modern_name: canonical rational structure / descent of the universal abelian cover compatible with S_3
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in Ihara's and Anderson's work

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates a uniqueness conjecture. A group-theoretic characterization (conditions a, b, c) singles out a unique S_3-equivariant Q-structure on the universal abelian cover of P^1−3 points, and the Fermat tower realizes it. This is an independent route to the abelian layer of what Ihara studied via Jacobi sums in the same period.
missed.quote: Mais d'autre part la tour des revêtements de Fermat nous fournit très explicitement un tel objet
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The point is mainly historical: Grothendieck reached the Fermat-tower / abelian-layer viewpoint independently, around the same time as Ihara. The mathematics itself is essentially covered by Ihara–Anderson–Coleman.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a genuine but modest unpublished detail. Grothendieck independently uses the Fermat tower to realize the S_3-equivariant abelian cover of P^1−3 points over Q, and notes that it revealed the semidirect splitting. The content overlaps substantially with Ihara's mid-1980s work, so it is not new mathematics, though the S_3-equivariant uniqueness formulation is a nice unrecorded touch.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'deux semi-diagr[?]' should read 'deux scindages' (two splittings).
'G_{q,σ}' is most likely 'G_{ρ,σ}' (as on the previous page), with a tilde.
'sauf erreur[?] uniques[?] près' is likely 'à isom. unique près' (up to unique isomorphism).
'un rev. prorev.[?]' is likely 'un pro-revêtement' / 'un rev. pro-étale'.
'en n° 11' may be 'en n° 116' or a nearby number; the digits are unclear.
'M = M_{0,3}' denotes the curve/stack P^1 − 3 points (or its π1), not the module M.
